cim: When Elon Musk warned about the dangers of AI
cim_eredeti: When Elon Musk warned about the dangers of AI
szoveg_eredeti:
On January 16, 2017, Elon Musk posted the following message on Twitter, before it was called X and before he owned it: "Rewatched 'Ghost in the Shell' and the end of 'Colossus: The Forbin Project.'" The billionaire entrepreneur added a link to watch Colossus, an American feature film by Joseph Sargent released in 1970, for free on YouTube.

While Ghost in the Shell (1995), a Japanese animated film by Mamoru Oshii, depicted a world where robots and enhanced humans coexist, Colossus centers on a supercomputer named Colossus, tasked with overseeing the United States' nuclear arsenal. The machine made impressive advances, far beyond what its creator had anticipated, and took the initiative to launch a nuclear missile at the Soviet Union.

In a televised message addressed to all of humanity, the supercomputer ultimately imposed a new world order: "Obey me and live, or disobey and die." Now master of the world, it promised that under its rule, famine, disease and overpopulation would disappear – while eliminating individual freedoms in the process.

In his post, Musk drew attention to the film's terrifying ending, conceived at a time when the general public had little understanding of the potential implications of advances in computing. Years before American tech leaders – such as Sam Altman, co-founder and CEO of OpenAI, and Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic – began calling for a slowdown in AI development for fear that the technology could escape human control, Musk was already sounding the alarm. By 2024, however, he named the world's largest AI supercomputer, developed by his artificial intelligence company XAI (which notably developed the GROK AI model), Colossus, in tribute to the film.
